symbols.name: d
symbols.def: Fixed dimension of the innovation lattice.

symbols.name: \mathbb L
symbols.def: Innovation lattice \(\mathbb L=\mathbb Z^d\).

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: Generic displacement in the innovation lattice.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Number of observed vertices.

symbols.name: V_n
symbols.def: Connected periodic or Følner observation window with \(|V_n|=n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal M
symbols.def: Measurable space of observed vertex and edge marks.

symbols.name: \mathcal Y
symbols.def: Measurable space carrying the compatible finite-window potential-outcome functions and their stationary infinite-volume versions indexed by \(\mathbb L\).

symbols.name: \Omega
symbols.space: \(\mathcal U^{\mathbb L}\times\mathcal U^{\mathbb L}\times\mathsf{Graph}(\mathbb L)\times\mathcal M^{\mathbb L}\times\mathcal Y\times\{0,1\}^{\mathbb L}\times\{0,1\}^{\mathbb L}\)
symbols.def: One canonical infinite-volume sample space whose coordinates are the innovation field and its coupling copy, the graph and marks, the finite- and infinite-volume potential-outcome environment, and two assignment fields.

symbols.name: \mathcal A
symbols.def: Product sigma-field on \(\Omega\).

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: Common positive moment slack.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Exponent \(q=\delta/(2+\delta)\) used in shell--dependence summability.

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Generic common upper-envelope constant for the model class.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Generic common positive lower or exponential-decay constant.

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.def: Common geometric decay factor.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: Lower bound for Bernoulli assignment probabilities.

symbols.name: \epsilon
symbols.def: Arbitrary positive tolerance used in probability-convergence criteria.

symbols.name: \pi_0
symbols.def: Lower bound for the two target exposure probabilities.

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: First innovation-coordinate map \(U=(U_z)_{z\in\mathbb L}\) on \(\Omega\), containing the site and finite-range edge innovations.

symbols.name: U'
symbols.def: Independent copy of \(U\) used for physical-dependence couplings.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Annealed probability measure on the single joint space \(\left(\Omega,\mathcal A\right)\); all graph, mark, potential-outcome, innovation, and assignment objects below are coordinate maps or measurable functions on this same space.

symbols.name: G_\infty
symbols.def: Infinite-volume undirected graph generated from \(U\) by the translation-equivariant graph rule.

symbols.name: M_\infty
symbols.def: Infinite-volume observed mark field generated jointly from \(U\) by the translation-equivariant environment rule.

symbols.name: Y_i
symbols.def: For \(i\in V_n\), the finite-window coordinate \(d_0\mapsto Y_i(d_0)\) of the potential-outcome environment on \(\Omega\), using the declared restriction or periodic boundary convention.

symbols.name: Y_z^\infty
symbols.def: Stationary infinite-volume potential-outcome coordinate \(d_0\mapsto Y_z^\infty(d_0)\) at \(z\in\mathbb L\), generated with \(G_\infty\) and \(M_\infty\) from \(U\).

symbols.name: G_n
symbols.def: Observed restriction or periodic approximation of \(G_\infty\) on \(V_n\).

symbols.name: d_G
symbols.def: Shortest-path distance in \(G_\infty\), with the same notation used for the restricted distance in \(G_n\) on \(V_n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_n
symbols.def: Sub-sigma-field of \(\mathcal A\) generated by \(G_n\), \(M_\infty\) restricted to \(V_n\), and \(\{Y_i:i\in V_n\}\); it contains no assignment coordinate.

symbols.name: \mathcal F_\infty
symbols.def: Sub-sigma-field \(\mathcal F_\infty=\sigma(U,G_\infty,M_\infty,(Y_z^\infty)_{z\in\mathbb L})\subset\mathcal A\), containing the full environment and no assignment coordinate.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Known Bernoulli assignment probability.

symbols.name: D_\infty
symbols.def: Assignment-coordinate field \(D_\infty=(D_z)_{z\in\mathbb L}\) on \(\Omega\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Observed treatment vector \(D=(D_i)_{i\in V_n}=D_\infty|_{V_n}\).

symbols.name: D'
symbols.def: Restriction to \(V_n\) of the second assignment coordinate on \(\Omega\), coupled to be an independent conditional copy of \(D\) given \(\mathcal F_n\).

symbols.name: D^{(i,s)}
symbols.def: Assignment equal to \(D\) on \(\{j:d_G(i,j)\le s\}\) and to \(D'\) outside that ball.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Fixed graph radius of the exposure mapping.

symbols.name: T_i
symbols.def: Graph-local exposure \(T_i=T(i,D,G_n)\).

symbols.name: T_z^\infty
symbols.def: Stationary graph-local exposure \(T_z^\infty=T(z,D_\infty,G_\infty)\) at \(z\in\mathbb L\), compatible with the finite-window exposure away from the boundary.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: First exposure in the causal contrast.

symbols.name: t'
symbols.def: Second exposure in the causal contrast.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Generic member of the two target exposures.

symbols.name: \pi_i(a)
symbols.def: Exact design probability \(\pi_i(a)=\Pr\{T_i=a\mid\mathcal F_n\}\).

symbols.name: \pi_z^\infty(a)
symbols.def: Infinite-volume design probability \(\pi_z^\infty(a)=\Pr_P\{T_z^\infty=a\mid\mathcal F_\infty\}\).

symbols.name: Z_i
symbols.def: Score \(Z_i=Y_i(D)\{\mathbf 1(T_i=t)/\pi_i(t)-\mathbf 1(T_i=t')/\pi_i(t')\}\).

symbols.name: Z_z^\infty
symbols.def: Infinite-volume score \(Z_z^\infty=Y_z^\infty(D_\infty)\{\mathbf 1(T_z^\infty=t)/\pi_z^\infty(t)-\mathbf 1(T_z^\infty=t')/\pi_z^\infty(t')\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_n
symbols.def: Estimator \(\widehat\tau_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}Z_i\).

symbols.name: m_i
symbols.def: Finite-window conditional mean \(m_i=\mathbb E_P[Z_i\mid\mathcal F_n]\), with every object defined on \(\left(\Omega,\mathcal A,P\right)\).

symbols.name: m_z^\infty
symbols.def: Infinite-volume conditional mean \(m_z^\infty=\mathbb E_P[Z_z^\infty\mid\mathcal F_\infty]\), including \(m_0^\infty\) at the distinguished origin.

symbols.name: \tau_n
symbols.def: Realized finite-network effect \(\tau_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}m_i\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Generic set of at most four Palm roots.

symbols.name: P^0
symbols.def: Origin-rooted law \(P^0(B)=P\{\omega:(\omega,0)\in B\}\). Because \(\mathbb L\) is deterministic, rooting distinguishes the origin without size biasing the environment.

symbols.name: \mathbb E^0
symbols.def: Expectation \(\mathbb E^0[X]=\int X\,\mathrm dP^0\) under the origin-rooted law.

symbols.name: P^A
symbols.def: Finite-root law \(P^A(B)=P\{\omega:(\omega,A)\in B\}\), which records the common environment together with the distinguished root set \(A\).

symbols.name: \mathbb E^A
symbols.def: Expectation \(\mathbb E^A[X]=\int X\,\mathrm dP^A\) under the finite-root law.

symbols.name: \tau_{\mathrm P}
symbols.def: Population target \(\tau_{\mathrm P}=\int m_0^\infty\,\mathrm dP^0=\mathbb E^0[m_0^\infty]\), where \(m_0^\infty=\mathbb E_P[Z_0^\infty\mid\mathcal F_\infty]\).

symbols.name: \xi_i
symbols.def: Assignment score \(\xi_i=Z_i-m_i\).

symbols.name: h_i
symbols.def: Environment score \(h_i=m_i-\tau_{\mathrm P}\).

symbols.name: h_z^\infty
symbols.def: Infinite-volume centered score \(h_z^\infty=m_z^\infty-\tau_{\mathrm P}\).

symbols.name: S_{\mathrm{des},n}
symbols.def: Design coordinate \(S_{\mathrm{des},n}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in V_n}\xi_i\).

symbols.name: S_{\mathrm{pop},n}
symbols.def: Population coordinate \(S_{\mathrm{pop},n}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in V_n}h_i\).

symbols.name: R_i^{\mathrm{stab}}
symbols.def: Smallest ambient radius outside which innovation changes do not alter the local graph, mark, and finite- or infinite-volume conditional-mean score at vertex \(i\).

symbols.name: a_s
symbols.def: Geometric envelope \(a_s=C\rho^s\).

symbols.name: v(s)
symbols.def: Deterministic common envelope for graph shells and balls at radius \(s\).

symbols.name: b_n
symbols.def: Possibly graph-measurable hard-cutoff bandwidth.

symbols.name: \Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}
symbols.def: Conditional variance \(\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}=\operatorname{Var}_P(S_{\mathrm{des},n}\mid\mathcal F_n)\).

symbols.name: \xi_z^\infty
symbols.def: Infinite-volume assignment-centered score \(\xi_z^\infty=Z_z^\infty-m_z^\infty\) at \(z\in\mathbb L\).

symbols.name: \Omega_{\mathrm{des}}
symbols.def: Palm covariance series \(\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}=\sum_{z\in\mathbb L}\mathbb E^0[\operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi_0^\infty,\xi_z^\infty\mid\mathcal F_\infty)]\).

symbols.name: \gamma_{\mathrm{pop}}(z)
symbols.def: Population covariance \(\gamma_{\mathrm{pop}}(z)=\mathbb E^0[h_0^\infty h_z^\infty]\) for \(z\in\mathbb L\).

symbols.name: \Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}
symbols.def: Population covariance series \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=\sum_{z\in\mathbb L}\gamma_{\mathrm{pop}}(z)\).

symbols.name: \Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}
symbols.def: Total variance \(\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Omega_n
symbols.def: Unchanged Leung hard-cutoff quadratic \(\widehat\Omega_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}(Z_i-\widehat\tau_n)(Z_j-\widehat\tau_n)\mathbf 1\{d_G(i,j)\le b_n\}\).

symbols.name: R_n
symbols.def: Remainder \(R_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}(m_i-\tau_n)(m_j-\tau_n)\mathbf 1\{d_G(i,j)\le b_n\}\).

symbols.name: Q_n(b_n)
symbols.def: Population-mean-centered cutoff quadratic \(Q_n(b_n)=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}h_ih_j\mathbf 1\{d_G(i,j)\le b_n\}\).

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: Nominal two-sided test size.

symbols.name: \Phi
symbols.def: Standard normal distribution function.

symbols.name: \mathrm{CI}_{n,\alpha}
symbols.def: Interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,\alpha}=[\widehat\tau_n\pm\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\sqrt{\widehat\Omega_n/n}]\).

symbols.name: B_i
symbols.def: Bernoulli chord coordinate contained in \(U\) in the explicit local-chord witness.

symbols.name: H_i
symbols.def: Centered mark \(H_i=B_i-1/2\).

symbols.name: X^\star
symbols.def: Constant observed covariate field used to embed the local-chord witness into the network-exogeneity comparison.

symbols.name: \eta^\star
symbols.def: Comparator unobserved-heterogeneity field \(\eta_i^\star=H_i=B_i-1/2\) in the local-chord law.

symbols.name: S_i
symbols.def: Signed assignment \(S_i=2D_i-1\) in the explicit witness.

symbols.name: q_i
symbols.def: Witness degree \(q_i=2+B_i+B_{i-2}\).

symbols.name: P_\star
symbols.def: Joint infinite-volume law induced by the iid chord coordinates, their translation-equivariant graph, marks and potential outcomes, and the independent Bernoulli assignment field in the local-chord construction.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: Rademacher coordinate that is common to every vertex within row \(n\) of the nonergodic triangular boundary.

symbols.name: P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: For each \(n\ge3\), the product law having a Rademacher first coordinate \(Q\) and an independent second-coordinate field of iid \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) variables indexed by \(V_n\).

symbols.name: D_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Assignment coordinate at vertex \(i\in V_n\) under \(P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\).

symbols.name: S_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Signed row assignment \(S_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=2D_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}-1\).

symbols.name: G_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Deterministic cycle graph on \(V_n=\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\) in row \(n\).

symbols.name: d_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Shortest-path distance in the cycle \(G_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\).

symbols.name: b_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Deterministic row bandwidth \(b_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=\max\{1,\lfloor\log n\rfloor\}\).

symbols.name: T_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Direct-treatment exposure \(T_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=D_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}\).

symbols.name: Y_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Row potential outcome \(Y_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}(d_0)=1/2+Q(2d_{0,i}-1)/(2\sqrt n)\).

symbols.name: Z_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Direct-exposure IPW score \(Z_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=Y_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}((D_{n,j}^{\mathrm{cs}})_{j\in V_n})\{\mathbf 1(T_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=1)/(1/2)-\mathbf 1(T_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=0)/(1/2)\}=S_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}+Q/\sqrt n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Row environment sigma-field \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=\sigma(Q,G_n^{\mathrm{cs}})\), which excludes the assignment coordinates.

symbols.name: m_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Row conditional mean \(m_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=\mathbb E_{P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}}[Z_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}\mid\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cs}}]=Q/\sqrt n\).

symbols.name: \tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Deterministic row target \(\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=\mathbb E_{P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}}[m_{n,0}^{\mathrm{cs}}]=0\).

symbols.name: \overline m_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Realized row mean \(\overline m_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}m_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=Q/\sqrt n\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Row estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}Z_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Omega_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Row analogue of the unchanged sample-mean-centered graph-HAC estimator in Theorem 4 on p. 18 of the accessible 4 November 2021 arXiv manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI}: \(\widehat\Omega_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}(Z_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}-\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}})(Z_{n,j}^{\mathrm{cs}}-\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}})\mathbf 1\{d_n^{\mathrm{cs}}(i,j)\le b_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\}\).

symbols.name: R_n^{\mathrm{cs}}
symbols.def: Row analogue of Leung's heterogeneous-effect remainder, \(R_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}(m_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}-\overline m_n^{\mathrm{cs}})(m_{n,j}^{\mathrm{cs}}-\overline m_n^{\mathrm{cs}})\mathbf 1\{d_n^{\mathrm{cs}}(i,j)\le b_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}
symbols.def: Pointwise class of stationary ergodic local-innovation network-experiment laws defined below.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Arbitrary fixed finite threshold used in the uniform bandwidth-divergence criterion.

symbols.name: r_n
symbols.def: Common deterministic sequence with \(r_n\uparrow\infty\) used to localize the innovation sensitivity of the endogenous graph-distance selector.

symbols.name: U^{A,r}
symbols.def: Innovation field obtained from \(U\) by independently resampling the coordinates in the union of ambient radius-\(r\) neighborhoods of the roots in \(A\), leaving all other coordinates unchanged.

symbols.name: W_{ij,n}(U)
symbols.def: Selector \(W_{ij,n}(U)=\mathbf 1\{d_{G(U)}(i,j)\le b_n(U)\}\) generated by the same innovation field as the environment scores.

symbols.name: W_{ij,n}^{A,r}
symbols.def: Coupled selector \(W_{ij,n}^{A,r}=W_{ij,n}(U^{A,r})\), with both the generated graph and any graph-measurable bandwidth recomputed from \(U^{A,r}\).

symbols.name: \mathscr S_i(r)
symbols.def: Measurable endpoint score-support block \(\mathscr S_i(r)\subseteq\{z\in\mathbb L:\|z-i\|\le r\}\) whose innovations determine the radius-\(r\) truncation of the centered score at \(i\); the block may be strictly smaller than the ambient ball.

symbols.name: \ell_{ij}
symbols.def: Ambient separation \(\ell_{ij}=\|i-j\|\) between two endpoints.

symbols.name: \ell_n(i,j)
symbols.def: For \(i,j\in V_n=\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\), choose arbitrary integer lifts \(\widetilde i,\widetilde j\) and set \(\ell_n(i,j)=\min_{m\in\mathbb Z}|\widetilde i-\widetilde j+mn|\); the minimum is independent of the lifts.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm G}
symbols.def: Common upper constant in the geodesic-core revealment and anti-concentration condition.

symbols.name: c_{\mathrm G}
symbols.def: Common positive constant in the Gaussian curvature envelope of the geodesic-core revealment and anti-concentration condition.

symbols.name: \mu_{\mathrm G}
symbols.def: Deterministic centering speed for the revealed core passage count.

symbols.name: \mathscr R_{ij}^{\ell,r}
symbols.def: Measurable algorithm which explores a canonical \(i\)--\(j\) geodesic from its endpoint blocks toward an unrevealed core.

symbols.name: A_i^{ij}
symbols.def: Endpoint delay exposed by \(\mathscr R_{ij}^{\ell,r}\) from the block \(\mathscr S_i(r)\), with the paired delays satisfying \(|A_i^{ij}|+|A_j^{ij}|\le C_{\mathrm G}r\).

symbols.name: L_{ij}^{\ell,r}
symbols.def: Core passage count exposed by \(\mathscr R_{ij}^{\ell,r}\), independent of the innovations in \(\mathscr S_i(r)\cup\mathscr S_j(r)\) on the successful revealment event.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_i(r)
symbols.def: Standard-Borel measurable state space carrying the innovation block \(U|_{\mathscr S_i(r)}\) used by the endpoint revealment.

symbols.name: E_{ij}^{\ell,r}
symbols.def: Event that \(\mathscr R_{ij}^{\ell,r}\) successfully exposes the two endpoint delays and an endpoint-independent core passage count.

symbols.name: a_i^{ij}
symbols.def: Generic value in the essential support of the integer endpoint delay \(A_i^{ij}\).

symbols.name: F_{\ell,r}^{a_i,a_j}
symbols.def: On the essential support of \((A_i^{ij},A_j^{ij})\), \(F_{\ell,r}^{a_i,a_j}(k)=\Pr_P\{L_{ij}^{\ell,r}\le k\mid A_i^{ij}=a_i^{ij},A_j^{ij}=a_j^{ij},E_{ij}^{\ell,r}\}\) for \(\ell_{ij}=\ell\). Regular conditional versions on null endpoint-delay values are immaterial.

symbols.name: E_{ij,kl}^{\ell_1,\ell_2,r}
symbols.def: Event that both canonical revealments succeed, the four endpoint blocks are exposed, and the two revealed corridors do not overlap.

symbols.name: F^{(4),\mathbf a}_{\ell_1,\ell_2,r}
symbols.def: On the essential support of the four-delay vector \(\mathbf a=(a_i^{ij},a_j^{ij},a_k^{kl},a_l^{kl})\), the regular conditional bivariate cdf of the two core passage counts given all four delay values and \(E_{ij,kl}^{\ell_1,\ell_2,r}\). Kernel versions on null delay values are immaterial.

symbols.name: \Delta_u
symbols.def: For an integer-valued argument, \(\Delta_u f(t)=f(t+u)-f(t)\); products such as \(\Delta_u\Delta_v\) and \(\Delta_{u_1}\cdots\Delta_{u_4}\) denote signed mixed differences.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Generic integer threshold at which a revealed passage-count distribution is differenced.

symbols.name: \zeta_2(\ell,r)
symbols.def: Deterministic upper bound for failure of the two-endpoint canonical revealment at separation \(\ell\) and radius \(r\).

symbols.name: \zeta_4(\ell_1,\ell_2,r)
symbols.def: Deterministic upper bound for failure of the two-corridor four-endpoint revealment at separations \(\ell_1,\ell_2\) and radius \(r\), apart from corridor overlap.

symbols.name: Z_{2,n}(P,r)
symbols.def: Normalized failure sum \(Z_{2,n}(P,r)=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}\zeta_2(\ell_{ij},r)\mathbf 1\{d_G(i,j)\le b_n+C_{\mathrm G}r\}\).

symbols.name: Z_{4,n}(P,r)
symbols.def: Normalized sum \(Z_{4,n}(P,r)=n^{-2}\sum_{i,j,k,l\in V_n}\zeta_4(\ell_{ij},\ell_{kl},r)\mathbf 1\{d_G(i,j)\vee d_G(k,l)\le b_n+C_{\mathrm G}r\}\).

symbols.name: N_{4,n}(b,r)
symbols.def: Number of ordered quadruples \(i,j,k,l\in V_n\) for which both selectors lie within the cutoff front and the two canonical corridors revealed at radius \(r\) overlap.

symbols.name: \operatorname{shell}(b)
symbols.def: Deterministic envelope \(\operatorname{shell}(b)=\max_{0\le s\le C_{\mathrm G}b}v(s)\) for the graph shells intersecting a cutoff front of order \(b\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H_i(r)
symbols.def: Class \(\mathcal H_i(r)=\{f:f\text{ is measurable with respect to }U|_{\mathscr S_i(r)},\ \mathbb E_P[f]=0,\ \|f\|_{P,4+\delta}\le1\}\) of centered, normalized functions of the endpoint score-support block.

symbols.name: \Delta_{2,n}(P,r)
symbols.def: Signed coefficient \(\Delta_{2,n}(P,r)=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}\sup_{f_i\in\mathcal H_i(r),f_j\in\mathcal H_j(r)}|\mathbb E_P[f_if_j\sum_{B\subseteq\{i,j\}}(-1)^{2-|B|}W_{ij,n}^{B,r}]|\), with \(W_{ij,n}^{\varnothing,r}=W_{ij,n}(U)\).

symbols.name: \Delta_{4,n}(P,r)
symbols.def: For \(A=\{i,j,k,l\}\), \(\Delta_{4,n}(P,r)=n^{-2}\sum_{i,j,k,l\in V_n}\sup_{f_a\in\mathcal H_a(r),a\in A}|\mathbb E_P[(\prod_{a\in A}f_a)\sum_{B\subseteq A}(-1)^{4-|B|}W_{ij,n}^{B,r}W_{kl,n}^{B,r}]|\), with coincident roots merged and \(W^{\varnothing,r}=W(U)\).

symbols.name: \Delta_{\mathrm{app},n}(P)
symbols.def: Approximation modulus \(\Delta_{\mathrm{app},n}(P)=\|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in V_n}(\xi_i-\xi_i^\infty)\|_{P,2}+\|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in V_n}(h_i-h_i^\infty)\|_{P,2}+\|\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}-n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}\operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi_i^\infty,\xi_j^\infty\mid\mathcal F_\infty)\|_{P,1}\), using the declared embedding of \(V_n\) into \(\mathbb L\).

symbols.name: \mathcal Q
symbols.def: Fixed nonempty candidate family of pointwise laws over which common-rate conclusions are sought.

symbols.name: \mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}
symbols.def: Uniform subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\) defined below from \(\mathcal Q\).

symbols.name: o_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}(1)
symbols.def: Uniform stochastic order defined by the supremum-probability criterion below.

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm{BL}}
symbols.def: Bounded-Lipschitz metric \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{\|f\|_\infty+\operatorname{Lip}(f)\le1}|\int f\,\mathrm d\mu-\int f\,\mathrm d\nu|\).

symbols.name: \mathcal N_2
symbols.def: Bivariate Gaussian probability law indexed by its mean and positive-semidefinite covariance matrix.

symbols.name: \widehat\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}
symbols.def: Assignment-centered quadratic \(\widehat\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}\xi_i\xi_jW_{ij,n}(U)\).

symbols.name: A_{\mathrm G}
symbols.def: Fixed multiplier in the logarithmic-logarithmic GRAC revealment radius.

symbols.name: R_{\max}
symbols.def: Fixed maximum shortcut length in the bounded-range Newman--Watts family.

symbols.name: \underline p_{\mathrm{sw}}
symbols.def: Common lower bound separating optional-shortcut probabilities from zero and one.

symbols.name: \vartheta
symbols.def: Vector \(\vartheta=(\vartheta_2,\ldots,\vartheta_{R_{\max}})\) of independent optional-shortcut probabilities.

symbols.name: R_Y
symbols.def: Fixed ambient radius of the innovation block entering a bounded local outcome map.

symbols.name: \varphi
symbols.def: Bounded measurable map from the innovation block \((U_{z+u})_{\|u\|\le R_Y}\) and the assignment configuration \((d_x)_{d_G(x,z)\le K}\) to a real potential outcome; the map may be nonconstant in the edge-generating innovations.

symbols.name: \theta
symbols.def: Parameter \(\theta=(\vartheta,\varphi)\) collecting shortcut probabilities and a bounded local outcome map.

symbols.name: P_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NW}}
symbols.def: Stationary law indexed by \(\theta\) on a ring or fixed-width strip with a deterministic nearest-neighbor backbone, independent optional edges of lengths \(2,\ldots,R_{\max}\) having probabilities \(\vartheta\), potential outcomes generated by \(\varphi\), and an independent Bernoulli assignment field.

assumptions.condition: Under \(P\), the coordinates of \(U\) are independent and identically distributed.

standard.name: Independent and identically distributed innovation field

assumptions.condition: The measurable map from \(U\) to \(G_\infty\), \(M_\infty\), and \(Y_z^\infty\), together with its compatible finite-window objects \(G_n\) and \(Y_i\), commutes with lattice translations and the declared observation-window convention.
The graph \(G_n\) is connected with \(P\)-probability one for every \(n\).
Almost surely, \(\sup_{i\in V_n}|\{j\in V_n:d_G(i,j)=s\}|\le v(s)\) for every \(n\) and \(s\ge0\).
Under \(P\), conditionally on \(\mathcal F_\infty\), the coordinates of \(D_\infty\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) draws, and \(D=D_\infty|_{V_n}\).
Each \(T_i\) depends on \(D\) only through the \(K\)-ball of \(i\) in \(G_n\), and each \(T_z^\infty\) depends on \(D_\infty\) only through the \(K\)-ball of \(z\) in \(G_\infty\).
Almost surely, the minimum of \(\inf_{n\ge1}\inf_{i\in V_n}\min_{a\in\{t,t'\}}\pi_i(a)\) and \(\inf_{z\in\mathbb L}\min_{a\in\{t,t'\}}\pi_z^\infty(a)\) is at least \(\pi_0\).

The maximum of \(\sup_{n\ge1}\sup_{i\in V_n}\sup_{d_0\in\{0,1\}^{V_n}}\|Y_i(d_0)\|_{P,4+\delta}\) and \(\sup_{z\in\mathbb L}\sup_{d_0\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb L}}\|Y_z^\infty(d_0)\|_{P,4+\delta}\) is at most \(C\).
The assignment coupling obeys \(\sup_{n\ge1}\sup_{i\in V_n}\|Y_i(D)-Y_i(D^{(i,s)})\|_{P,2+\delta}\le a_s\) for every \(s\ge K\).

novel.justification: This geometric \(L^{2+\delta}\) ANI envelope is a strengthened moment version of approximate neighborhood interference. It implies the \(L^1\) ANI condition of \cite{Leung2022ANI} by norm monotonicity and \(a_s\to0\). It is satisfied by bounded local outcomes on finite-range interference neighborhoods, including outcomes that share innovations with the graph, because the coupled difference is then exactly zero beyond the interference radius.

assumptions.condition: Replacing \(U\) by \(U'\) outside the ambient radius \(r\) around a root changes either the compatible finite-window mean \(m_i\) or the infinite-volume mean \(m_z^\infty\) in \(L^{4+\delta}(P)\) by at most \(C\rho^r\).

novel.justification: This exponential exterior-resampling stability condition is imposed directly on conditional mean scores. Bounded local outcomes on bounded-range innovation graphs satisfy it with zero change once the exterior begins beyond the combined outcome and graph-interference radius. Single-site physical-dependence coefficients in \cite{ElMachkouriVolnyWu2013} are technique-level precedent, but do not themselves state this exterior-resampling property.

assumptions.condition: For every Palm law rooted at a set \(A\subset\mathbb L\) with \(|A|\le4\), \(\mathbb E^A[\exp\{c\max_{i\in A}R_i^{\mathrm{stab}}\}]\le C\).

standard.name: Exponential stabilization under multi-root Palm laws

assumptions.condition: For every \(z\in\mathbb L\) and \(s\ge1\), \(P^0\{d_G(0,z)\le s,\|z\|>Cs\}+P^0\{d_G(0,z)>s,\|z\|<cs\}\le C\exp[-c\max\{s,\|z\|\}]\).

novel.justification: This two-sided chemical-distance capture condition is satisfied deterministically by connected bounded-range lattice graphs with mandatory nearest-neighbor edges, including the local-chord cycle witness, and is natural for geometric graphs with exponential passage-time tails. It rules out bottlenecks and shortcuts that make graph distance unrelated to the innovation geometry while still allowing the cutoff and scores to share innovations.

assumptions.condition: The common envelopes obey \(\sum_{s=0}^{\infty}v(s)a_s^q<\infty\).
For each member law \(P\), the graph-measurable bandwidth satisfies \(b_n\to_P\infty\).
For each member law \(P\), the bandwidth and shell envelope satisfy \(v(b_n)^4/n\to_P 0\).
For each member law \(P\), the boundary loss obeys \(|\partial V_n|v(b_n)/n\to_P 0\).

standard.name: Følner boundary condition for covariance sums

assumptions.condition: For each member law \(P\), the annealed variance satisfies \(\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}(P)\ge c\).

standard.name: Uniform nondegeneracy of the normalized sum

assumptions.condition: For every fixed member law \(P\), \(\Delta_{\mathrm{app},n}(P)\to0\).

standard.name: Vanishing finite-window approximation for stabilizing functionals

assumptions.condition: For every fixed \(B<\infty\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\Pr_P\{b_n\le B\}\to0\).
For every \(\epsilon>0\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\Pr_P\{v(b_n)^4/n>\epsilon\}\to0\).
For every \(\epsilon>0\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\Pr_P\{|\partial V_n|v(b_n)/n>\epsilon\}\to0\).
The finite-/infinite-volume approximation modulus satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\Delta_{\mathrm{app},n}(P)\to0\).

standard.name: Uniform finite-window approximation for stabilizing functionals

assumptions.condition: For every fixed \(P\), endpoints \(i,j\), separation \(\ell=\ell_{ij}\), and radius \(r\), the endpoint states lie in standard-Borel spaces \(\mathcal E_i(r)\) and \(\mathcal E_j(r)\), almost every delay pair \((a_i^{ij},a_j^{ij})\) in the essential support satisfies \(\Pr_P(E_{ij}^{\ell,r}\mid A_i^{ij}=a_i^{ij},A_j^{ij}=a_j^{ij})\ge1-\zeta_2(\ell,r)>0\), and on \(E_{ij}^{\ell,r}\) the canonical shortest-path length equals \(A_i^{ij}+L_{ij}^{\ell,r}+A_j^{ij}\), where \(|A_i^{ij}|+|A_j^{ij}|\le C_{\mathrm G}r\), with the core count conditionally independent of the two endpoint blocks given the delay values.

novel.justification: Bounded-range small-world graphs with a mandatory backbone admit a left-to-right finite-state shortest-path exploration. Endpoint innovations determine only bounded delays, while the untouched interior supplies an independent passage count; this is directly checkable from the graph-generation rule.

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over all delay pairs \((a_i^{ij},a_j^{ij})\) in the essential support, all integers \(\kappa,u,v\), and \(\ell\ge1\), the regular conditional kernel obeys \(|\Delta_u\Delta_vF_{\ell,r}^{a_i,a_j}(\kappa)|\le C_{\mathrm G}(|u|+1)(|v|+1)\ell^{-1}\exp\{-c_{\mathrm G}(\kappa-\mu_{\mathrm G}\ell)^2/\ell\}+\zeta_2(\ell,r)\), with its values at null delay pairs unrestricted.

novel.justification: A finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov-additive shortest-path recursion has a spectral local limit theorem whose differentiated transfer kernel has exactly this discrete-curvature envelope. The restriction is on the passage kernel, not on outcomes or a variance target.

assumptions.condition: For two selectors with four standard-Borel endpoint blocks, the paired revealment exposes four delays and two core passage counts, almost every four-delay vector in the essential support has conditional successful-nonoverlap probability at least \(1-\zeta_4(\ell_1,\ell_2,r)>0\) given all four delay values, and on that event the two core counts are conditionally independent of the four endpoint blocks given those values.

novel.justification: In a bounded-range ring or strip, two shortest-path explorations use independent interiors unless their revealed corridors intersect. Corridor intersection is a geometric event that can be counted without reference to scores or the HAC quadratic.

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over every four-delay vector \(\mathbf a\) in the essential support, every fourth signed mixed difference of \(F^{(4),\mathbf a}_{\ell_1,\ell_2,r}\) is bounded by \(C_{\mathrm G}\prod_{a=1}^4(|u_a|+1)(\ell_1\ell_2)^{-1}\) times a centered bivariate Gaussian envelope with marginal scales \(\sqrt{\ell_1}\) and \(\sqrt{\ell_2}\), plus \(\zeta_4(\ell_1,\ell_2,r)\), with kernel versions at null four-delay values unrestricted.

novel.justification: The two-distance transfer matrix of a finite-range passage process yields the required fourth discrete derivative uniformly on compact shortcut-probability sets. This condition is an observable graph-law smoothness restriction and contains no score or inferential conclusion.

assumptions.condition: For every fixed \(P\), the GRAC error modulus \(r_n^2/\sqrt{b_n}+r_n^4/b_n+N_{4,n}(b_n,r_n)/n^2+Z_{2,n}(P,r_n)+Z_{4,n}(P,r_n)+\operatorname{shell}(b_n)^2\rho^{r_n}\) converges to zero in \(P\)-probability.

novel.justification: The rate is checkable from shortest-path corridor geometry. With logarithmic bandwidth, logarithmic-logarithmic revealment radius, bounded-range shortcuts, and exponential score stabilization, each term vanishes while the graph selector may retain nonzero one-endpoint pivotal probability.

assumptions.condition: The supremum over \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}\) of the probability that \(r_n^2/\sqrt{b_n}+r_n^4/b_n+N_{4,n}(b_n,r_n)/n^2+Z_{2,n}(P,r_n)+Z_{4,n}(P,r_n)+\operatorname{shell}(b_n)^2\rho^{r_n}\) exceeds any fixed positive threshold converges to zero.

novel.justification: Compact bounded-range small-world parameter families have common spectral gaps, local-limit constants, and corridor-count bounds, so the same revealment calculation is uniform without restricting outcomes by an inferential target.

definitions.name: Pointwise stabilizing annealed network-experiment class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}=\{P\in\mathcal P(\Omega,\mathcal A):P\text{ and its restrictions to every }V_n\text{ satisfy the iid-environment, translation-equivariance, connectedness, shell-envelope, Bernoulli-design, exposure-locality, exposure-positivity, outcome-moment, ANI-coupling, score-stabilization, four-root-stabilization, chemical-compatibility, shell-summability, bandwidth-divergence, bandwidth-growth, Folner-boundary, total-nondegeneracy, and finite-volume-approximation conditions with the same deterministic }d,\delta,C,c,\rho,\varepsilon,\pi_0,K,v,a_s,r_n\}\).

definitions.name: Uniform stabilizing annealed network-experiment subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}=\{P\in\mathcal Q:P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\text{ and }\mathcal Q\text{ satisfies uniform bandwidth divergence, uniform bandwidth growth, the uniform Folner boundary condition, and uniform finite-volume approximation with the common deterministic tuple }d,\delta,C,c,\rho,\varepsilon,\pi_0,K,v,a_s,r_n\}\).

definitions.name: Geodesic-core revealment and anti-concentration condition
definitions.construction: A graph rule and bandwidth satisfy GRAC when endpoint blocks take values in standard-Borel spaces and a canonical shortest-path revealment separates bounded endpoint delays from an endpoint-independent core passage count. Conditional success is at least \(1-\zeta_2\) almost everywhere on the essential delay support, the regular conditional kernels \(F_{\ell,r}^{a_i,a_j}\) obey the declared second-difference Gaussian curvature bound uniformly over supported delays, and the analogous four-delay kernel \(F^{(4),\mathbf a}_{\ell_1,\ell_2,r}\), conditioned on successful nonoverlapping revealment, obeys the declared fourth mixed-difference bound. Kernel versions at null delay values are immaterial, and the normalized revealment-failure and corridor-overlap modulus vanishes.

definitions.name: Uniform GRAC condition
definitions.construction: A family in \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}\) satisfies uniform GRAC when the same revealment construction and constants \(C_{\mathrm G},c_{\mathrm G},\mu_{\mathrm G}\) apply to every member and the declared GRAC error modulus vanishes in supremum probability.

definitions.name: Signed mixed-endpoint coefficients
definitions.construction: For each endpoint block use centered \(L^{4+\delta}(P)\)-normalized functions and apply the signed second mixed difference of one selector or the signed fourth mixed difference of a product of two selectors under endpoint-block resampling. Average the resulting absolute coefficients as the declared \(\Delta_{2,n}(P,r)\) and \(\Delta_{4,n}(P,r)\). Zeroth- and first-order selector effects are absent by construction.

definitions.name: Finite-/infinite-volume CLT approximation modulus
definitions.construction: Couple finite- and infinite-volume scores on \(\Omega\) and compute \(\Delta_{\mathrm{app},n}(P)\) as the sum of the \(L^2(P)\) discrepancies of the normalized design and population sums and the \(L^1(P)\) discrepancy between the finite conditional variance and its infinite-volume covariance sum.

definitions.name: Uniform convergence in probability
definitions.construction: A family \(X_n(P)\) is \(o_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}(1)\) exactly when, for every \(\epsilon>0\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}\Pr_P\{|X_n(P)|>\epsilon\}\to0\).

definitions.name: Palm population exposure effect
definitions.construction: At the origin of the rooted infinite-volume law, form \(Z_0^\infty=Y_0^\infty(D_\infty)\{\mathbf 1(T_0^\infty=t)/\pi_0^\infty(t)-\mathbf 1(T_0^\infty=t')/\pi_0^\infty(t')\}\), set \(m_0^\infty=\mathbb E_P[Z_0^\infty\mid\mathcal F_\infty]\), and define \(\tau_{\mathrm P}=\int m_0^\infty\,\mathrm dP^0\).

definitions.name: Exposure-IPW score and estimator
definitions.construction: For \(i\in V_n\), compute the exact design probabilities \(\pi_i(t)\) and \(\pi_i(t')\), set \(Z_i=Y_i(D)\{\mathbf 1(T_i=t)/\pi_i(t)-\mathbf 1(T_i=t')/\pi_i(t')\}\), and return \(\widehat\tau_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}Z_i\).

definitions.name: Design--population score decomposition
definitions.construction: Set \(m_i=\mathbb E_P[Z_i\mid\mathcal F_n]\), \(\xi_i=Z_i-m_i\), \(h_i=m_i-\tau_{\mathrm P}\), \(S_{\mathrm{des},n}=n^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i\), and \(S_{\mathrm{pop},n}=n^{-1/2}\sum_i h_i\).

definitions.name: Palm variance components
definitions.construction: Compute the absolutely convergent Palm covariance series \(\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}=\sum_{z\in\mathbb L}\mathbb E^0[\operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi_0^\infty,\xi_z^\infty\mid\mathcal F_\infty)]\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=\sum_{z\in\mathbb L}\mathbb E^0[h_0^\infty h_z^\infty]\), then set \(\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\).

definitions.name: Unchanged graph-distance HAC and Leung remainder
definitions.construction: Using the hard cutoff from the observed graph, compute \(\widehat\Omega_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j}(Z_i-\widehat\tau_n)(Z_j-\widehat\tau_n)\mathbf 1\{d_G(i,j)\le b_n\}\) and \(R_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i,j}(m_i-\tau_n)(m_j-\tau_n)\mathbf 1\{d_G(i,j)\le b_n\}\).

definitions.name: GRAC implication and failure-search handle
definitions.construction: Reveal a canonical shortest path from endpoint score-support blocks into an independent passage core; obtain second and fourth discrete cdf curvature from a finite-state transfer matrix or a local limit theorem, sum the Gaussian cutoff front over ambient separations, and count overlapping corridor pairs. To test whether GRAC follows from the base class primitives alone, search connected bounded-range factor graphs for a passage kernel with a persistent mixed cutoff-front atom; use ambient-distance HAC if such a law exists.

definitions.name: Connected iid-local-chord cycle witness
definitions.construction: Take \(d=1\) and \(\mathbb L=\mathbb Z\). Draw iid \(B_z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) as coordinates of \(U\); in \(G_\infty\), retain every nearest-neighbor edge and add the undirected chord \(\{z,z+2\}\) exactly when \(B_z=1\). Let \(G_n\) be the periodic quotient on \(V_n=\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\) for \(n\ge5\), with any fixed admissible connected prefix for \(n<5\). Independently draw \(D_\infty\) with \(D_z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), take \(t=1\), \(t'=0\), \(T_i=D_i\), and set \(Y_z^\infty(D_\infty)=H_zD_z+(4q_z)^{-1}\sum_{j:j\sim z}D_j\), with \(Y_i\) its periodic restriction, \(H_z=B_z-1/2\), and \(q_z=2+B_z+B_{z-2}\). This construction induces \(P_\star\).

definitions.name: Stationary nonergodic common-shock triangular boundary
definitions.construction: For each \(n\ge3\), set \(V_n=\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\), let \(G_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\) be its deterministic cycle, and use the row law \(P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\) under which \(Q\) is Rademacher and \(D_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}\) are iid \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independent of \(Q\). Set \(t=1\), \(t'=0\), \(T_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=D_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}\), and \(Y_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}(d_0)=1/2+Q(2d_{0,i}-1)/(2\sqrt n)\). Then \(Z_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=S_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}+Q/\sqrt n\), \(m_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=Q/\sqrt n\), \(\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=\mathbb E_{P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}}[m_{n,0}^{\mathrm{cs}}]=0\), and \(\overline m_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=Q/\sqrt n\). Use \(b_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=\max\{1,\lfloor\log n\rfloor\}\) in the row analogues \(\widehat\Omega_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\) and \(R_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\) of the unchanged estimator and remainder in Theorem 4 on p. 18 of the accessible 4 November 2021 arXiv manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI}.

definitions.name: Bounded-range Newman--Watts graph family
definitions.construction: Fix \(R_{\max}\ge2\), \(R_Y<\infty\), and \(K<\infty\). On a ring or fixed-width strip retain the deterministic nearest-neighbor backbone and, independently for every admissible displacement \(k=2,\ldots,R_{\max}\), add the optional edge with probability \(\vartheta_k\in[\underline p_{\mathrm{sw}},1-\underline p_{\mathrm{sw}}]\). For any bounded measurable, possibly nonconstant map \(\varphi\), set \(Y_z^\infty(d)=\varphi((U_{z+u})_{\|u\|\le R_Y},(d_x)_{d_G(x,z)\le K})\), use compatible periodic restrictions, and attach an independent Bernoulli assignment field. The parameter \(\theta=(\vartheta,\varphi)\) induces \(P_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NW}}\).

statements.statement: For every \(n\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_{\mathrm P})=S_{\mathrm{des},n}+S_{\mathrm{pop},n}\), \(\mathbb E_P[S_{\mathrm{des},n}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0\), and \(\mathbb E_P[S_{\mathrm{des},n}S_{\mathrm{pop},n}]=0\). The last equality is finite-sample orthogonality, not an asymptotic covariance restriction.
statements.justification: The exact split identifies assignment and graph-population uncertainty before any limit argument.
statements.gap: \cite{AbadieAtheyImbensWooldridge2020} separates design and sampling uncertainty for regression, while \cite{Leung2022ANI} conditions on one fixed graph and potential-outcome schedule; neither gives this exposure-score split on a random local network.
statements.consumer: The split gives the two coordinates needed to report how much uncertainty in a one-network experiment is due to treatment assignment versus network-population variation.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\), both Palm covariance series in \(\mathrm{def:variance\mbox{-}components}\) converge absolutely, \(\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}(P)\), and \(n^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_P(\sum_{i\in V_n}h_i)\to\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)\). Consequently \(n\operatorname{Var}_P(\widehat\tau_n)\to\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}(P)\).
statements.justification: The variance limits must be derived from primitive stabilization and shell conditions rather than inserted as assumptions.
statements.gap: Proposition 2 and Theorem 1 of \cite{ElMachkouriVolnyWu2013} derive covariance summability and a random-field variance limit, but not the conditional assignment variance coupled to a generated graph.
statements.consumer: This result supplies interpretable design and population variance shares for annealed causal reporting.

statements.statement: For every \(\epsilon>0\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}\Pr_P\{|\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}-\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}(P)|>\epsilon\}\to0\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}|n^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_P(\sum_{i\in V_n}h_i)-\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)|\to0\); the Palm covariance tails are absolutely summable under the common envelopes.
statements.justification: Uniform Gaussian approximation and studentization require familywise convergence of the two variance coordinates, not merely memberwise limits.
statements.gap: The stationary-field variance limits in \cite{ElMachkouriVolnyWu2013} and the conditional network limits in \cite{KojevnikovMarmerSong2021} do not combine uniform finite-window coupling with a generated graph environment.
statements.consumer: The uniform joint CLT uses these limits to index its Gaussian comparison law by the correct member-specific covariance matrix.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\), shell summability and \(b_n\to_P\infty\) imply \(\sum_{s>b_n}v(s)a_s^q\to_P 0\).
statements.justification: The omitted covariance tail is a consequence of summability and bandwidth divergence, not an independent restriction on the model class.
statements.gap: Network-HAC statements often list tail control separately; here monotone deterministic tails show it is redundant under the declared pointwise primitives.
statements.consumer: Every pointwise truncation argument in the variance, GRAC, and HAC proofs uses this corollary instead of an extra class assumption.

statements.statement: For every \(\epsilon>0\), common shell summability and uniform bandwidth divergence imply \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}\Pr_P\{\sum_{s>b_n}v(s)a_s^q>\epsilon\}\to0\).
statements.justification: A deterministic tail cutoff converts the familywise bandwidth-divergence condition into the omitted-tail bound uniformly.
statements.gap: The uniform tail requirement is frequently imposed as a separate bandwidth condition even when a common summable envelope makes it derivable.
statements.consumer: Uniform quadratic and studentization arguments use this corollary without shrinking the uniform law family by a redundant premise.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\) and fixed \(u\in\mathbb R\), \(\mathbb E_P[\exp(iuS_{\mathrm{des},n})\mid\mathcal F_n]-\exp\{-u^2\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}(P)/2\}\to_P 0\), and \((S_{\mathrm{des},n},S_{\mathrm{pop},n})\Rightarrow(N_{\mathrm{des},P},N_{\mathrm{pop},P})\), where the coordinates are independent centered Gaussian variables with variances \(\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}(P)\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)\). Hence \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_{\mathrm P})\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}(P))\), allowing either component, but not their sum, to vanish.
statements.justification: A conditional characteristic-function limit plus a stabilizing-field CLT establishes genuine joint independence rather than mere zero covariance.
statements.gap: Theorem 3 (Asymptotic Normality) on p. 14 of the accessible 4 November 2021 arXiv manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI} is design-based around a fixed-network exposure effect, and Theorem 3 of \cite{LiWager2022} gives a model-specific graphon population CLT; neither produces a quenched--annealed two-coordinate limit for ANI exposure-IPW on one sparse stabilizing graph.
statements.consumer: The theorem permits a Palm-population interpretation of exposure effects from a single expanding randomized network.

statements.statement: Do the base pointwise assumptions defining \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\), without the GRAC conditions, imply the existence of a geodesic-core revealment whose two-root and nonoverlapping four-root regular conditional kernels satisfy the declared supported-delay curvature and error-decay bounds? Do their uniform counterparts imply common GRAC constants and uniform error decay? If either implication fails, construct a stationary connected exponentially stabilizing law satisfying the remaining conditions whose signed mixed cutoff-front coefficient persists.
statements.justification: This isolates whether ordinary stabilization and chemical-distance capture already force the checkable shortest-path transfer-kernel condition, without making that unresolved implication a dependency of exactness.
statements.gap: Theorem 4.2 on pp. 27--28 of \cite{Leung2019b} assumes network exogeneity, and Proposition 4.1 of \cite{KojevnikovMarmerSong2021} begins from conditional centering; neither derives mixed endpoint curvature for a shortest-path selector generated with the score field.
statements.consumer: A positive answer removes GRAC as an extra condition; a counterexample supplies a sharp diagnostic for replacing graph distance by ambient spatial distance.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\) satisfying GRAC, endpoint resampling and conditional centering give \(\Delta_{2,n}(P,r_n)\le C_{\mathrm G}[r_n^2/\sqrt{b_n}+Z_{2,n}(P,r_n)+\operatorname{shell}(b_n)\rho^{r_n}]\) and \(\Delta_{4,n}(P,r_n)\le C_{\mathrm G}[r_n^4/b_n+N_{4,n}(b_n,r_n)/n^2+Z_{4,n}(P,r_n)+\operatorname{shell}(b_n)^2\rho^{r_n}]\). Hence both signed coefficients converge to zero under \(\mathrm{ass:grac\mbox{-}error\mbox{-}decay}\).
statements.justification: The lemma turns checkable shortest-path revealment and curvature into exactly the signed two- and four-root coefficients consumed by the endogenous quadratic law.
statements.gap: Existing network-HAC coupling arguments bound absolute selector changes; they do not exploit conditional centering to cancel zeroth- and first-order endpoint effects through discrete passage-kernel curvature.
statements.consumer: The pointwise and uniform endpoint-quadratic lemmas consume these bounds directly, so no pivotality limit is assumed as a premise.

statements.statement: For a family satisfying uniform GRAC, every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}\) obeys \(\Delta_{2,n}(P,r_n)\le C_{\mathrm G}[r_n^2/\sqrt{b_n}+Z_{2,n}(P,r_n)+\operatorname{shell}(b_n)\rho^{r_n}]\) and \(\Delta_{4,n}(P,r_n)\le C_{\mathrm G}[r_n^4/b_n+N_{4,n}(b_n,r_n)/n^2+Z_{4,n}(P,r_n)+\operatorname{shell}(b_n)^2\rho^{r_n}]\), with the same constant. Consequently, \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}\Pr_P\{\Delta_{2,n}(P,r_n)+\Delta_{4,n}(P,r_n)>\epsilon\}\to0\) for every \(\epsilon>0\).
statements.justification: This separates the familywise selector bound from its pointwise counterpart and preserves common GRAC constants throughout the supremum-probability argument.
statements.gap: No existing network-HAC result supplies uniform signed mixed-endpoint bounds for two shortest-path selectors driven by the score innovations.
statements.consumer: The uniform endpoint-quadratic lemma uses this result without importing any pointwise-only or unconditional open-question dependency.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\) satisfying GRAC, the signed endpoint bounds from \(\mathrm{lem:grac\mbox{-}implies\mbox{-}pivotality}\), Hölder score truncation, and the two-selector four-root law of large numbers give \(Q_n(b_n)\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)\), \(R_n\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)\), and \(n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}\xi_i h_jW_{ij,n}(U)\to_P 0\).
statements.justification: This lemma is the bridge from signed GRAC coefficients, now derived rather than assumed, to the three quadratic limits needed by the unchanged HAC expansion.
statements.gap: Proposition 4.1 of \cite{KojevnikovMarmerSong2021} controls a conditionally centered network-HAC quadratic, but does not handle a selector, conditional means, and bandwidth generated by the same innovations.
statements.consumer: The pointwise exact-HAC theorem uses these limits without depending on the open question of whether the older primitives imply GRAC.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\) satisfying GRAC, \(\widehat\Omega_n=\widehat\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}+R_n+o_P(1)\), \(\widehat\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}(P)\), \(R_n\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)\), and therefore \(\widehat\Omega_n\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}(P)\). Conditional on GRAC and its derived signed endpoint lemma, this strictly tightens Theorem 4 (Variance Estimator) on p. 18 and Remark 2 on p. 17 of the accessible 4 November 2021 arXiv manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI}: the same sample-mean-centered graph HAC is exact for the Palm target, reduces to its design variance when \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)=0\), and has \(R_n\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)>0\) on the local-chord law.
statements.justification: The result converts Leung's fixed-population heterogeneity remainder into the missing superpopulation variance without changing the reported standard error.
statements.gap: Preprint Theorem 4 and Remark 2 of \cite{Leung2022ANI} leave the superpopulation behavior of \(R_n\) model-dependent. Theorem 4.2 of \cite{Leung2019b} obtains path-distance HAC validity under network exogeneity. The conditional tightening here allows shared graph--outcome innovations under GRAC, whose signed endpoint control is derived from a shortest-path transfer kernel.
statements.consumer: Applied users of exposure-IPW can retain the familiar graph-HAC workflow while changing its interpretation from conservative realized-network inference to exact Palm-population inference.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(u\in\mathbb R\) and \(\epsilon>0\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}\Pr_P\{|\mathbb E_P[\exp(iuS_{\mathrm{des},n})\mid\mathcal F_n]-\exp[-u^2\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}(P)/2]|>\epsilon\}\to0\). Moreover, \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}d_{\mathrm{BL}}(\mathcal L_P(S_{\mathrm{des},n},S_{\mathrm{pop},n}),\mathcal N_2(0,\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}(P),\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P))))\to0\).
statements.justification: The uniform bounded-Lipschitz formulation supplies the precise familywise Gaussian approximation needed for honest studentization.
statements.gap: The accessible preprint Theorem 3 of \cite{Leung2022ANI} is a pointwise fixed-schedule CLT; quantitative stabilization results do not combine its conditional assignment coordinate with a uniform Palm population coordinate.
statements.consumer: This is the numerator approximation used by the uniform Wald coverage theorem.

statements.statement: Under uniform GRAC, uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}\), \(Q_n(b_n)-\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)=o_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}(1)\), \(R_n-\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P)=o_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}(1)\), and \(n^{-1}\sum_{i,j\in V_n}\xi_i h_jW_{ij,n}(U)=o_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}(1)\).
statements.justification: Common transfer-kernel constants, uniform revealment errors, shell truncation, and four-root averaging yield the familywise quadratic bridge.
statements.gap: Existing network-HAC results do not provide a uniform law for a two-selector four-root term with a graph-measurable endogenous bandwidth.
statements.consumer: The uniform exact-HAC theorem and uniform Wald theorem require this familywise quadratic control.

statements.statement: Under uniform GRAC, \(\widehat\Omega_n-\widehat\Omega_{\mathrm{des},n}-R_n=o_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}(1)\) and, for every \(\epsilon>0\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}\Pr_P\{|\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}(P)|>\epsilon\}\to0\).
statements.justification: This separates pointwise exactness from the stronger operator-level uniform consistency claim.
statements.gap: Neither the fixed-population variance estimator theorem in \cite{Leung2022ANI} nor Proposition 4.1 of \cite{KojevnikovMarmerSong2021} gives supremum-probability consistency for shared-innovation graph weights.
statements.consumer: Uniform variance consistency is the denominator input for familywise Wald coverage.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), under uniform GRAC and \(\inf_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}(P)\ge c\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}}|\Pr_P\{\tau_{\mathrm P}(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,\alpha}\}-(1-\alpha)|\to0\).
statements.justification: Uniform studentized Gaussian approximation, uniform HAC consistency, and a common positive variance lower bound yield the operational population-coverage claim.
statements.gap: \cite{GaoDing2025} demonstrates possible anti-conservativeness of network-HAC inference and supplies a conservative modification; it does not identify a random-network class on which Leung's unchanged studentizer is uniformly exact for a Palm effect.
statements.consumer: This theorem supplies honest repeated-network population coverage for large online and field experiments whose realized network is one draw from a stable local population.

statements.statement: For the law \(P_\star\) in \(\mathrm{def:local\mbox{-}chord\mbox{-}witness}\), fix \(t=1\), \(t'=0\), and the explicit tuple \(d=1\), \(\delta=2\), \(q=1/2\), \(C=64\), \(c=1/8\), \(\rho=1/2\), \(\varepsilon=1/4\), \(\pi_0=1/2\), \(K=1\), \(p=1/2\), \(v(s)=4\), \(a_s=64\cdot2^{-s}\), \(b_n=\max\{1,\lfloor\log(n+1)\rfloor\}\), \(A_{\mathrm G}=16\), \(r_n=\lceil16\log\log(n+3)\rceil\), \(C_{\mathrm G}=10^6\), \(c_{\mathrm G}=10^{-6}\), and \(\mu_{\mathrm G}=2/3\). Then \(P_\star\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\): the innovations are iid; every graph is connected and has shells of size at most four; exposure probabilities equal \(1/2\); \(\sup|Y_i|\le3/4\); the strengthened \(L^{2+\delta}\) ANI difference is zero for \(s\ge1\); graph and conditional-mean-score exterior-resampling changes are zero beyond radius two; \(d_G(i,j)\le\ell_n(i,j)\le2d_G(i,j)\); shell summability, bandwidth growth, the Følner condition, and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{app},n}(P_\star)\le64n^{-1/2}\) hold, while \(\Omega_{\mathrm{ann}}=3721/6144\ge c\). The omitted tail tends to zero by \(\mathrm{prop:bandwidth\mbox{-}tail}\). On the infinite lattice, for \(i<j\) and \(\ell=|i-j|\), the shortest-path length is \(\ell\) minus the maximum matching size in \(B_i,\ldots,B_{j-2}\). The finite endpoint-state spaces are standard Borel, the canonical revealment succeeds with conditional probability one for every supported delay pair, and the delay-conditioned kernels \(F_{\ell,r}^{a_i,a_j}\) are therefore well defined on their essential support. The matching recursion is an irreducible aperiodic two-state Markov-additive chain whose transfer matrix gives \(\sup_k\Pr\{d_G(i,j)=k\}=O(\ell^{-1/2})\), \(\sup_k|\Pr\{d_G(i,j)=k+1\}-\Pr\{d_G(i,j)=k\}|=O(\ell^{-1})\), and the corresponding supported-delay two-distance fourth-difference bound, verifying GRAC with the displayed constants. Once \(b_n<n/4\), the unique short-arc selector does not reveal terminal \(B_j\), whereas \(h_j=B_j-1/2\); hence \(\Delta_{2,n}(P_\star,r_n)=0\) for distinct endpoints. Among \(O(nb_n)\) selected pairs each corridor overlaps only \(O(b_n^2)\) others, so \(\Delta_{4,n}(P_\star,r_n)=O(b_n^3/n)\). The general GRAC bounds are \(O((\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})\) and \(O((\log\log n)^4/\log n+(\log n)^3/n)\); score truncation is zero whenever \(r_n\ge2\). Finally, \(m_i=H_i\), \(\tau_{\mathrm P}=0\), \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=1/4\), \(\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}=2185/6144\), \(Q_n(b_n)\to_{P_\star}1/4\), and \(R_n\to_{P_\star}1/4\). With \(X_i^\star=0\) and \(\eta_i^\star=H_i\), the law violates the network-exogeneity premise of Theorem 4.2 in \cite{Leung2019b}.
statements.justification: One fully quantified connected heterogeneous law verifies class nonvacuity, the signed GRAC mechanism, the variance arithmetic, and strict separation from exogenous-network path-HAC theory.
statements.gap: Theorem 4.2 and Remark 4.3 of \cite{Leung2019b} exclude this shared-innovation law through network exogeneity; existing deterministic-ring HAC examples do not derive the transfer-kernel curvature or centered endpoint cancellation.
statements.consumer: The closed-form values give a reproducible unit test for simulations and for the eventual proof's normalization and centering conventions.

statements.statement: The class \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\) is not contained in the network-exogenous domain of Theorem 4.2 in \cite{Leung2019b}. In particular, \(P_\star\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\), but under the embedding \(X^\star_i=0\) and \(\eta_i^\star=H_i=B_i-1/2\), the nondegenerate unobserved heterogeneity \(\eta^\star\) is measurable from the chord indicators in \(G_\infty\), and therefore \(\eta^\star\not\!\perp\!\!\!\perp G_\infty\mid X^\star\). The same law has deterministic stabilization radius at most two and satisfies \(d_G(i,j)\le\ell_n(i,j)\le2d_G(i,j)\), so it obeys the proposal's stabilization and chemical-distance conditions.
statements.justification: The explicit non-representability result prevents path-distance HAC exactness under network exogeneity from being mistaken for the shared-innovation theorem proposed here.
statements.gap: Theorem 4.2 on pp. 27--28 of \cite{Leung2019b} imposes network exogeneity, and Remark 4.3 on p. 29 explains its role; that paper does not give validity for a graph and heterogeneous outcome score generated by the same local innovation.
statements.consumer: A referee can use this witness to distinguish the proposed theorem's model domain from the closest existing path-distance HAC theorem before assessing the random-metric lemma.

statements.statement: For each \(n\ge3\), the row law \(P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\) in \(\mathrm{def:common\mbox{-}shock\mbox{-}witness}\) is invariant under cyclic vertex shifts and is nonergodic because the nondegenerate variable \(Q\) is shift invariant. This triangular sequence is outside \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\), whose members are single stationary ergodic infinite-volume laws. Under \(P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\), \(m_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}=\overline m_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=Q/\sqrt n\), \(\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=0\), and \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}}-\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}})=Q+n^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in V_n}S_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}\Rightarrow \tfrac12\mathcal N(-1,1)+\tfrac12\mathcal N(1,1)\); in particular, \(n\operatorname{Var}_{P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}}(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}})=2\) for every \(n\). Sample centering gives the exact identity \(Z_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}-\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=S_{n,i}^{\mathrm{cs}}-n^{-1}\sum_{j\in V_n}S_{n,j}^{\mathrm{cs}}\), so it removes \(Q/\sqrt n\) from every summand. Consequently, \(R_n^{\mathrm{cs}}=0\) for every \(n\) and the row analogue \(\widehat\Omega_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\) of Leung's unchanged sample-mean-centered graph-HAC estimator in Theorem 4 on p. 18 of the accessible 4 November 2021 arXiv manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI} satisfies \(\widehat\Omega_n^{\mathrm{cs}}\to_{P_n^{\mathrm{cs}}}1\). Thus that named estimator captures the iid assignment variance but misses the order-one variance \(\operatorname{Var}(Q)=1\) of the invariant population component on this boundary.
statements.justification: The explicit row-by-row construction isolates the variance component erased by sample centering and shows exactly where ergodicity enters population studentization.
statements.gap: Theorem 4 on p. 18 and Remark 2 on p. 17 of the accessible 4 November 2021 arXiv manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI} analyze the unchanged sample-mean-centered graph-HAC estimator for a fixed finite population, while \cite{Dedecker1998} permits invariant-sigma-field mixture limits; neither computes this estimator's probability limit against the annealed variance on a stationary nonergodic triangular boundary.
statements.consumer: Analysts can use the variance-one discrepancy to recognize when Leung's reported graph-HAC standard error requires repeated independent networks or an explicit model for an invariant shock.

statements.statement: Sanity corollary, already known from the homogeneous-effect discussion on printed p. 16 of the accessible version 4 manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI}: if \(m_i=\tau_{\mathrm P}\) almost surely for every \(i\), then the bookkeeping definitions immediately give \(h_i=0\), \(S_{\mathrm{pop},n}=0\), \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\), and \(R_n=0\). The score decomposition therefore contains only the fixed-population design coordinate. Dense direct-effect sequences of the type studied by \cite{LiWager2022} are only an analogous assignment-dominated boundary when their population projection vanishes; they are not members of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\) by this corollary.
statements.justification: This is a sanity-only bookkeeping reduction, not a theorem contribution.
statements.gap: The zero-remainder homogeneous boundary is already recorded on printed p. 16 of the accessible version 4 manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI}; the corollary only checks that the annealed notation reduces to it.
statements.consumer: The criterion prevents analysts from adding a spurious population component when conditional exposure effects are homogeneous.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(R_{\max},R_Y,K<\infty\), every shortcut vector \(\vartheta\in[\underline p_{\mathrm{sw}},1-\underline p_{\mathrm{sw}}]^{R_{\max}-1}\), and every bounded measurable map \(\varphi\), the local outcomes \(Y_z^\infty(d)=\varphi((U_{z+u})_{\|u\|\le R_Y},(d_x)_{d_G(x,z)\le K})\) under \(P_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NW}}\) obey the geometric \(L^{2+\delta}\) ANI condition with coupled difference exactly zero for \(s\ge K\). Exterior innovation resampling changes \(m_z^\infty\) and its compatible finite-window version by exactly zero once \(r\ge R_Y+R_{\max}K\). Choosing \(\varphi\) nonconstant in an innovation coordinate that also generates an edge gives a continuum of heterogeneous endogenous graph--outcome laws satisfying both strengthened conditions.
statements.justification: The proposition proves that the two strengthened dependence conditions cover a continuum of nonconstant shared-innovation laws rather than only the isolated local-chord witness.
statements.gap: The \(L^1\) ANI condition in \cite{Leung2022ANI} and the single-site physical-dependence coefficients in \cite{ElMachkouriVolnyWu2013} do not provide this exact finite-range verification for conditional mean scores on an endogenous graph.
statements.consumer: Applied bounded-range transport and communication-network models can verify the strengthened score assumptions directly from their local outcome code before attempting the separate GRAC transfer-matrix check.

statements.statement: For fixed \(R_{\max}\) and \(\vartheta\in[\underline p_{\mathrm{sw}},1-\underline p_{\mathrm{sw}}]^{R_{\max}-1}\), the shortest-hop process under every \(P_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NW}}\) is a finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov-additive passage process whose graph law depends only on \(\vartheta\). Its transfer matrix yields delay-conditioned GRAC two-root and nonoverlapping four-root curvature bounds with constants uniform in \(\vartheta\) and over supported endpoint-delay values; each selected pair has a corridor of order \(b_n\), so \(N_{4,n}(b_n,r_n)=O_P(nb_n^3)\). Consequently, with \(b_n=\lfloor\log(n+1)\rfloor\) and \(r_n=\lceil A_{\mathrm G}\log\log(n+3)\rceil\) for sufficiently large fixed \(A_{\mathrm G}\), this bounded-range small-world graph family satisfies uniform GRAC. The one-dimensional \(R_{\max}=2\), \(\vartheta_2=1/2\) graph member contains \(P_\star\).
statements.justification: The proposition supplies a recognizable applied graph family, not only an isolated witness, on which the new metric condition is verifiable by a finite transfer matrix.
statements.gap: Classical Newman--Watts work studies graph distances and small-world scaling, while network-HAC theory does not provide signed endpoint-curvature bounds for a graph metric sharing innovations with causal heterogeneity.
statements.consumer: A ring, fixed-width transport corridor, or communication network with a mandatory local backbone can be screened for exact annealed graph-HAC inference using finite-range shortcut diagnostics.

sampling_model.design: One joint infinite-volume law \(P\) on \(\left(\Omega,\mathcal A\right)\) carries iid innovations, the generated graph and outcomes, and assignments conditionally iid Bernoulli given \(\mathcal F_\infty\). Pointwise inference ranges over \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\); familywise inference uses \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}\). The strengthened geometric \(L^{2+\delta}\) ANI and exterior-resampling score conditions are verified for bounded nonconstant local outcomes on bounded-range Newman--Watts graphs. Exact graph-metric studentization additionally requires pointwise or uniform GRAC, verified separately from the outcome conditions by the shortest-path transfer matrix.
sampling_model.units: Vertices in connected periodic or Følner windows \(V_n\subset\mathbb Z^d\) with \(|V_n|=n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditionally independent \(D_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), with exact graph-local exposure probabilities for \(t\) and \(t'\).
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform assignment overlap \(p\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) and exposure positivity \(\pi_i(a)\ge\pi_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No statistical nuisance is estimated: the randomization law and exposure probabilities are known. The only tuning object is the observed-graph bandwidth \(b_n\).

target_estimand: \(\tau_{\mathrm P}=\int m_0^\infty\,\mathrm dP^0=\mathbb E^0[\mathbb E_P(Z_0^\infty\mid\mathcal F_\infty)]\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: In the accessible 4 November 2021 arXiv manuscript, Theorem 2 on p. 13 proves consistency, Theorem 3 on p. 14 proves the fixed-finite-population ANI CLT, and Theorem 4 on p. 18 gives the sample-centered graph-HAC decomposition; Remark 2 on p. 17 leaves the remainder's superpopulation behavior model-dependent. Under GRAC, Theorem 2 of this proposal strictly tightens that variance-estimator conclusion for a Palm target.

Theorem 4.2 on pp. 27--28 establishes consistency of a path-distance network-HAC estimator under first-order stationarity, a path-distance condition, network exogeneity, kernel regularity, and the relevant central-limit assumptions; Remark 4.3 on p. 29 explains that network exogeneity prevents omitted conditional covariance across disconnected agents.
Proposition 4.1 proves network-HAC consistency for conditionally centered or common-conditionally-mean network-dependent arrays under shell, dependence, and bandwidth restrictions.
The paper shows that a design-based network-HAC covariance estimator may be anti-conservative and constructs a positive-semidefinite asymptotically conservative modification.

The direct-effect theorem gives root-(n) Gaussian limits around sample and population targets under a graphon model and notes that the population-target variance adds a heterogeneity component that is difficult to estimate.
The regression framework separates sampling-based and design-based uncertainty and characterizes when robust standard errors coincide with or exceed the relevant variance.
Exposure-mapping Horvitz--Thompson estimators are design-unbiased, admit conservative randomization variance estimation, and have local-dependence asymptotic normality for fixed potential outcomes.

tldr: On one joint infinite-volume law carrying iid innovations, a generated sparse graph and outcomes, and Bernoulli assignments, the exposure-IPW error splits into orthogonal assignment and Palm-population coordinates. The geometric \(L^{2+\delta}\) ANI envelope and exponential exterior-resampling stability of conditional mean scores are strengthened conditions, not attributions to prior work; bounded nonconstant local outcomes on a compact bounded-range Newman--Watts family verify both, even when outcome heterogeneity shares edge innovations. Exactness of Leung's unchanged sample-mean-centered graph HAC is separately conditional on GRAC, now stated through regular delay-conditioned kernels on standard-Borel endpoint spaces. Under GRAC, \(\widehat\Omega_n\) estimates \(\Omega_{\mathrm{des}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), \(R_n\) estimates \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), and uniform Wald intervals cover the Palm effect. The local-chord calculation, a nonergodic common shock, and the already-known homogeneous reduction provide verification and boundary checks; the Bond et al. Facebook experiment motivates a population reanalysis subject to the diagnostics.

project_justification.gap: Remark 2 and Theorem 4 of the accessible preprint of \cite{Leung2022ANI} leave the superpopulation remainder model-dependent, while Theorem 4.2 of \cite{Leung2019b} relies on network exogeneity. Neither controls centered conditional means and a shortest-path cutoff generated by shared innovations. Leung's \(L^1\) ANI condition and standard single-site physical-dependence coefficients also do not imply the strengthened moment and exterior-resampling conditions used here.
project_justification.niche: A signed mixed-endpoint condition can isolate the genuine second- and fourth-order selection terms, provided its conditional passage kernels are well defined on the supported endpoint states. Bounded local outcome maps furnish a broad endogenous family for the strengthened score conditions, while finite-state shortest-path revealment independently makes GRAC checkable.
project_justification.fill: The project derives pointwise and uniform quenched--annealed limits, proves GRAC-to-pivotality bounds from supported-delay transfer-kernel curvature and corridor counts, feeds those bounds into the endogenous quadratic lemma, and then establishes conditional exactness and Wald coverage. A separate applicability proposition verifies the strengthened ANI and score-stability conditions for a continuum of bounded nonconstant local outcomes. The local-chord calculation and common-shock boundary supply nonvacuity and failure checks; the homogeneous corollary is retained only as an already-known sanity reduction.

related_work: The accessible arXiv:1911.07085v4 manuscript of \cite{Leung2022ANI} provides the exact estimator comparator: Theorem 2 on printed p. 13 is consistency, Theorem 3 on printed p. 14 is the fixed-schedule ANI central limit theorem, the homogeneous-effect reduction is discussed on printed p. 16, Remark 2 on printed p. 17 discusses the model-dependent superpopulation behavior of \(R_n\), and Theorem 4 on printed p. 18 establishes the sample-mean-centered graph-HAC decomposition. The DOI record confirms Econometrica 90(1), pp. 267--293; all theorem numbering here is explicitly the preprint's. Conditional on GRAC and its derived signed endpoint bounds, exactness strictly tightens preprint Theorem 4 by identifying the same remainder with Palm-population variance. The geometric \(L^{2+\delta}\) ANI envelope is stronger than Leung's \(L^1\) ANI premise by norm monotonicity, and the exterior-resampling condition on conditional mean scores is a new restriction rather than a Leung or random-field theorem. The closest path-distance comparator is Theorem 4.2 on pp. 27--28 of \cite{Leung2019b}; its network-exogeneity premise excludes the local-chord law because chord innovations also determine outcome heterogeneity, as Remark 4.3 on p. 29 anticipates. Proposition 4.1 of \cite{KojevnikovMarmerSong2021} informs shell and four-tuple bounds but does not handle a selector and scores generated by the same innovations. \cite{NewmanWatts1999} supplies the bounded-range small-world graph template; the proposed transfer-matrix theorem concerns delay-conditioned GRAC kernels, while a separate proposition verifies the strengthened score assumptions for bounded nonconstant local outcomes. \cite{ElMachkouriVolnyWu2013} supplies technique-level precedent through single-site physical-dependence coefficients, not the exterior-resampling premise; \cite{BaryshnikovYukich2005} and \cite{PenroseYukich2005} inform stabilization, Palm limits, and Gaussian approximation. \cite{AbadieAtheyImbensWooldridge2020} supplies the design-versus-population interpretation. \cite{GaoDing2025} shows why design asymptotics alone do not justify uniform network-HAC coverage. \cite{LiWager2022} gives a dense graphon population-target limit but no exact feasible Palm studentizer for this sparse local-innovation setting. \cite{AronowSamii2017} fixes exposure-IPW semantics. \cite{Dedecker1998} supplies the adjacent invariant-sigma-field mixture perspective. The ambient-distance estimators of \cite{Conley1999Spatial} and \cite{KelejianPrucha2007} remain the fallback if GRAC fails. \cite{WeinsteinNevo2026} and \cite{AuerbachGuoTabordMeehan2026} concern network misspecification and local response estimation rather than annealed variance. \cite{BondEtAl2012} supplies the proposed 61-million-user population-inference reanalysis; its network must pass the GRAC and stabilization diagnostics before the theorem applies.
technical_internal_limitation: GRAC is a primitive shortest-path revealment and transfer-kernel condition, but pivotality is no longer assumed: the signed coefficients are conclusions of \(\mathrm{lem:grac\mbox{-}implies\mbox{-}pivotality}\). Centering removes zeroth- and first-order endpoint effects, so total selector-change probability may remain nonzero. The endogenous quadratic lemma and every theorem remain to be proved. The OEQ asks whether the older stabilization and chemical-distance assumptions imply GRAC; it is not a dependency of exactness or coverage. If a legal connected stabilizing graph has a persistent signed mixed cutoff-front coefficient, the project must use ambient spatial-distance HAC. The hard graph cutoff can be indefinite in finite samples, so only asymptotic consistency and coverage are claimed.
honest_scope: Every statement has status \(\mathrm{to\mbox{-}prove}\). Pointwise CLT and variance claims concern each fixed \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{pt}}\); uniform claims concern only \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm u}\), with explicit supremum-probability bandwidth, boundary, and finite-window rates. Exact-HAC and Wald claims are conditional on GRAC and on proving the signed endpoint and quadratic lemmas; the OEQ is not their premise. The geometric \(L^{2+\delta}\) ANI and exterior-resampling score conditions are novel strengthenings, with applicability proved for bounded local Newman--Watts outcomes separately from GRAC. The omitted-tail limits are derived corollaries. The local-chord member and bounded-range Newman--Watts family are proposed GRAC verification theorems. The homogeneous boundary is an already-known sanity corollary, not a contribution. The common-shock sequence lies outside the single-law ergodic class and targets only Leung's unchanged sample-centered estimator. Dense graphon sequences are not members of the sparse class. The Facebook application remains a proposed reanalysis of \cite{BondEtAl2012} contingent on data access and verification of stabilization, bounded-range passage, overlap, and nondegeneracy.
